incident_text: Users say their balances are out of date: trades made more than ten minutes ago do not show up.

E-001.claim: portfolio-svc cache_staleness_s over 11:00-13:00 peaked at 1800 s, with the last sample also at 1800 s and a mean of 832.5 s.
E-001.author: observability

E-002.claim: portfolio-svc error rate stayed in a low band (min 0.002, max 0.004) across the window.
E-002.author: observability

E-003.claim: portfolio-svc latency averaged 120.068 ms over the window, with a max of 130.149 ms.
E-003.author: observability

E-004.claim: portfolio-consumer error rate stayed low (min 0.002, max 0.004, last 0.004).
E-004.author: observability

E-005.claim: portfolio-consumer latency mean was 162.724 ms with a max of 190.197 ms.
E-005.author: observability

E-006.claim: First portfolio-consumer WARN in the window: an update was reported as having no changes, and these WARNs recur through 12:56:51Z (20 lines total, no ERROR lines returned).
E-006.excerpt: 2026-03-30T11:17:47Z WARN portfolio-consumer: update 583 had no changes
E-006.author: observability

E-007.claim: First portfolio-svc WARN in the window is a holdings cache miss at 11:03:02Z; 18 such WARNs total, the last at 12:55:56Z.
E-007.excerpt: 2026-03-30T11:03:02Z WARN portfolio-svc: cache miss for holdings key 136270
E-007.author: observability

E-008.claim: rabbitmq looked healthy over the window: err_rate 0.0 and mean latency 1.991 ms.
E-008.author: observability

E-009.claim: Possibly the consumer is receiving trade updates that it considers already applied or empty, so portfolio-updates messages may not be carrying the new trade changes. This is unverified and needs the message payloads or the queue metrics.
E-009.author: observability

E-010.claim: Cache misses on holdings keys in portfolio-svc, together with the staleness metric hitting its 1800 s ceiling, may mean the read path serves cached holdings that are not refreshed after trades. This is unverified; no cache-refresh logs were queried.
E-010.author: observability

E-011.claim: The rise in portfolio-consumer latency (mean 162.7 ms vs portfolio-svc 120.1 ms) may be a secondary symptom and is not clearly abnormal without a baseline.
E-011.author: observability

E-012.claim: portfolio-updates queue depth stayed near zero over the window, with a max of 1.283 and a last value of 0.0.
E-012.author: observability

E-013.claim: Publish rate and consume rate were close, with consume rate slightly higher on average, so the queue was not backing up.
E-013.author: observability

E-014.claim: Consumer count was steady at 3 and the dead-letter queue stayed at zero.
E-014.author: observability

E-015.claim: Redeliveries were low but non-zero, with a mean of 0.272 and a max of 0.375.
E-015.author: observability

E-016.claim: portfolio-consumer error rate was low (mean 0.003, max 0.004), and its throughput was steady at about 40 rps.
E-016.author: observability

E-017.claim: portfolio-consumer latency per message was elevated compared with the rest of the path, with a mean of 162.7 ms and a max of 190.2 ms. This is a summary and not a per-message breakdown.
E-017.author: observability

E-018.claim: Postgres showed no connection pool saturation and write latency near 8 ms, which does not support a DB bottleneck.
E-018.author: observability

E-019.claim: Postgres replication lag was about 0.4 s and slow queries averaged about 1 per interval, so neither is large.
E-019.author: observability

E-020.claim: portfolio-consumer emitted only WARN lines in the window, with no ERROR lines. Each was 'update N had no changes', and 20 total were returned without truncation. The first was at 11:17:47Z and the last at 12:56:51Z.
E-020.excerpt: 2026-03-30T12:56:51Z WARN portfolio-consumer: update 464928 had no changes
E-020.author: observability

E-021.claim: RabbitMQ summary metrics show no error rate, with the error rate at 0.0 throughout. Its latency was about 2 ms and rps about 200. Queue-level metrics were not in this summary.
E-021.author: observability

E-022.claim: The 'had no changes' WARNs may mean the consumer received updates for which the DB had no change to apply, possibly dropping real balance changes. This is unverified and needs checking against the message payloads and the portfolio rows.
E-022.author: observability

E-028.author: dependency

E-029.claim: portfolio-consumer consumes from portfolio-updates and calls aa-sync (weight 0.8); no change was recorded for either.
E-029.author: dependency

E-030.claim: [Past incident INC-0412, hypothesis only, not evidence for this incident] Late balance notifications were previously tied to a Redis-related cache stampede on portfolio-svc.

E-030.author: dependency

E-039.author: dependency

E-042.author: dependency

E-044.author: dependency

E-047.claim: INC-0388 (2025-12-09) is a weaker match: account-aggregator data fetch failures for one bank, caused by bank-side FIP downtime and fixed by retry with backoff. It does not describe stale balances across users.
E-047.excerpt: "summary":"Account aggregator data fetch failures for one bank","root_cause":"Bank-side FIP downtime","fix":"Retried with backoff after the provider recovered"
E-047.author: dependency

E-048.claim: INC-0388 most plausibly relates to aa-sync, since its summary describes account-aggregator fetches. The record does not name a service.
E-048.author: dependency

E-049.claim: cache_staleness_s was 0.0 at every sample from 11:00 to 11:55, so it was not elevated before 12:00 at 5-minute resolution. This weakens the hint's premise that staleness predates the TTL change.
E-049.author: observability

E-050.claim: Staleness first became non-zero at the 12:00 sample, at 540 s, which is below 600 s. The earliest deviation is bracketed between 11:55 and 12:00.
E-050.author: observability

E-051.claim: Staleness first exceeded 600 s at the 12:05 sample, about 5 minutes after the 12:00 TTL change. The exact crossing time between 12:00 and 12:05 cannot be resolved at this step.
E-051.author: observability

E-052.claim: Staleness hit the 1800 s ceiling at 12:10 and remained there through the last sample at 12:55, matching the new TTL value.
E-052.author: observability

E-053.claim: Portfolio-svc served holdings from cache with entry age 180s at 12:00:22, the first cache-serve line in the window. Entry ages then increase in steps to 1800 s.
E-053.excerpt: 2026-03-30T12:00:22Z INFO portfolio-svc: serving holdings from cache, entry age 180s
E-053.author: observability

E-054.claim: Entry age reached the 1800 s TTL ceiling in the logs by 12:09:18 and was still 1800 s in the last cache-serve line, at 12:59:50.
E-054.excerpt: 2026-03-30T12:09:18Z INFO portfolio-svc: serving holdings from cache, entry age 1800s
E-054.author: observability

E-055.claim: Eleven holdings-cache misses were logged before 12:00 (11:03:02 to 11:57:28). Seven more followed after 12:00, 18 in total, so misses are sparse and their pre-12:00 baseline is unknown.
E-055.excerpt: 2026-03-30T11:03:02Z WARN portfolio-svc: cache miss for holdings key 136270
E-055.author: observability

E-056.claim: Redis hit ratio over the window had a minimum of 0.908 and a mean of 0.975, with a last value of 0.995. This summary has no time series, so when any dip occurred cannot be seen.
E-056.author: observability

E-057.claim: Redis evicted_keys was zero throughout the window, so there is no eviction signal. This weakens the INC-0412-style Redis-eviction hypothesis for this incident.
E-057.author: observability

E-058.claim: Previous-day cache_staleness_s for 2026-03-29 10:30–13:00 returned no points, with stats all null, although missing is reported as 0. No prior-day comparison is available from this metric.
E-058.author: observability

E-059.claim: A narrower previous-day query (2026-03-29 11:30–12:30) also returned no points. The empty result is not evidence that staleness was zero.
E-059.author: observability

E-060.claim: An entry age of 180 s at 12:00:22 is longer than the pre-change 60 s TTL. The entry was filled around 11:57 (after the 11:57:28 miss), so the new TTL may have applied before the logged 12:00 change, or the config record time is off. This ordering is suspicious and unverified.
E-060.author: observability

E-061.claim: Staleness jumps from 0 at 11:55 to 540 at 12:00, while logged entry ages climb gradually from 180 s. The metric and the logs may measure different quantities (for example, max staleness versus sampled entry age), so they are not directly reconciled.
E-061.author: observability

E-062.claim: The TTL change is the most likely driver of the staleness rise at 12:00–12:10. Redis evictions are zero, so cache pressure does not explain it. A pre-12:00 TTL effect cannot be excluded at this resolution.
E-062.author: observability

E-063.claim: Update 583 was logged only as a WARN with no changes, at 11:17:47Z, the first of the recurring WARNs.
E-063.excerpt: 2026-03-30T11:17:47Z WARN portfolio-consumer: update 583 had no changes
E-063.author: observability

E-064.author: observability

E-065.author: observability

E-066.author: observability

E-067.claim: A postgres DEBUG search for 'update' over 11:15-11:20 returned no lines, so no write was logged around update 583's onset.
E-067.author: observability

E-068.claim: The 'had no changes' path probably skips the postgres write, so the update may not have changed holdings. This is inferred from the log wording and the missing write line and is not verified.
E-068.author: observability

E-069.claim: Because update 583 has no processed line and no postgres write, the consumer may have discarded a real trade rather than applying it. This is unverified and needs payload contents and the affected account's holdings rows.
E-069.author: observability

E-074.author: dependency

E-076.author: dependency

E-077.author: dependency

E-078.claim: Trades probably reach aa-sync through a path not present in the graph (for example, broker-gateway feeding aa-sync via a non-listed edge or queue), or the graph is incomplete. This cannot be confirmed from the topology alone.
E-078.author: dependency

E-079.claim: The aa-sync to portfolio-consumer loop (publish to portfolio-updates, then synchronous call back to aa-sync) may mean that a delay in aa-sync slows the portfolio-updates feed as well as the consumer. This is inferred from the edges and has not been tested.
E-079.author: dependency

E-086.author: dependency

E-087.author: dependency

E-088.claim: redis-cache has no recorded changes of any kind (deploy, config, migration, flag) in the 11:00-13:00 window, so no Redis-side configuration change is recorded for holdings keys.
E-088.author: dependency

E-089.author: dependency

E-090.claim: Holdings keys in Redis take their TTL from portfolio-svc's HOLDINGS_CACHE_TTL_S setting at write time, so keys written after 12:00 should carry a 1800 s TTL. Keys written before 12:00 would keep the old TTL until they expire or are rewritten. This is inferred and not checked against Redis.
E-090.author: dependency

H1.statement: The 12:00 UTC change that raised HOLDINGS_CACHE_TTL_S on portfolio-svc from 60 s to 1800 s lets the holdings cache serve entries for up to 30 minutes, so balance reads omit trades older than ten minutes even though the write path works.

H2.statement: portfolio-consumer treats some portfolio-updates messages as 'no changes' and skips them, so real trade changes never reach postgres and balances stay stale at the source.

H3.statement: aa-sync, the only listed producer of portfolio-updates, publishes stale or incomplete trade data, or trades from broker-gateway and order-router never reach it, so a healthy downstream pipeline is fed old data.

T1.goal: Establish the timeline of the stale-balance problem: when did portfolio data first stop reflecting new trades? Collect error rates, latency and log anomalies for portfolio-svc, portfolio-consumer, broker-gateway, order-router and aa-sync from about 2 hours before the first user report until now, and identify the earliest point where behavior deviates from baseline.
hints: Compare against the same window on previous days
Look for the first error or warning log lines per service
Check whether trade execution (order-router, broker-gateway) is still succeeding while only the portfolio view is stale
T1.summary: Portfolio-side warnings appear before the 12:30 report: portfolio-svc logs holdings cache misses from 11:03:02Z, and portfolio-consumer logs 'update ... had no changes' warnings from 11:17:47Z, about 20 in the window. Metrics show cache_staleness_s peaking at 1800 with last=1800 and mean 832.5, but there are no time points, so the onset of staleness is unknown. No ERROR-level lines and no abnormal err_rate appear for these services, and rabbitmq looks healthy. Trade execution (order-router, broker-gateway) and baselines from previous days were not checked.

T2.goal: Examine the portfolio-updates queue on rabbitmq: queue depth, publish rate vs consume rate, consumer count, unacked messages, redelivery and dead-letter counts, and message age over time. Also check portfolio-consumer health (restarts, crashes, processing time per message, exceptions) and compare with inbound-msgs and outbound-msgs to see if the problem is isolated to portfolio-updates.
hints: Determine whether messages are not being published, not being consumed, or consumed but failing to write
Check postgres write latency, locks and connection pool saturation from portfolio-consumer
Check redis-cache hit rate, key TTLs and evictions for portfolio/balance keys, since stale reads could come from the cache
T2.summary: The portfolio-updates pipeline looks largely healthy at the summary level. Queue depth stayed near zero (mean 0.064, max 1.283, last 0.0), publish rate (mean 40.1/s) roughly matched consume rate (mean 46.0/s), there were 3 consumers throughout, and the DLQ was empty. Postgres showed no pool waiting and latency near 8 ms. The only WARN lines from portfolio-consumer are 20 'update N had no changes' messages, which could mean updates are being processed as no-ops, but I have not verified that. I could not establish a stall or write failure, and I did not use time-series points, so onset timing is unknown.

T3.goal: List every change of any kind in the 24 hours before the first stale-balance report: deploys, config changes, environment variable or secret changes, database migrations, feature flag flips, cache settings, rabbitmq topology or policy changes, scaling or infrastructure changes, and broker or account-aggregator credential or API changes. Give exact timestamps and the services affected, and flag those closest to the onset of the problem.
hints: Cover portfolio-svc, portfolio-consumer, broker-gateway, order-router, aa-sync, redis-cache, postgres, rabbitmq
Do not limit to deploys; include flags, config and migrations
Include changes made by third parties such as broker API version or rate limit changes if recorded
T3.summary: In the 24 hours before the 12:30 UTC report, get_changes (all kinds, unfiltered) recorded 4 changes. The one closest to onset is a config change on portfolio-svc at 12:00:00Z that raised HOLDINGS_CACHE_TTL_S from 60 to 1800, which would plausibly let cached holdings stay stale for up to 30 minutes. The three earlier changes are deploys on market-data, llm-gateway and broker-gateway between 11:19 and 11:27, which look unrelated to balance caching. No migrations, flag flips, rabbitmq, redis-cache, postgres, order-router, aa-sync or broker credential/API changes were recorded.

T4.goal: Map the service dependencies and queue links relevant to balance display: trace the path from a trade at broker-gateway/order-router through the portfolio-updates queue to portfolio-consumer, postgres and redis-cache, then to portfolio-svc and the orchestrator/wa-webhook/msg-delivery response path. Identify producers and consumers of each queue, shared resources (postgres, redis-cache, rabbitmq), and upstream sources such as aa-sync and market-data, so symptoms can be separated from causes.
hints: Note which components cache balances and with what TTL
Identify where each service could silently drop or delay an update
Note whether auth-kyc or llm-gateway sit in the balance read path
T4.summary: The only publisher of portfolio-updates in the graph is aa-sync, and broker-gateway shows no queue edges, so the trade path from broker-gateway/order-router to the queue is not confirmed. The strongest candidate is a portfolio-svc config change at 12:00 UTC that raised HOLDINGS_CACHE_TTL_S from 60 to 1800, a 30-minute TTL that would fit staleness beyond ten minutes, but portfolio-svc's place in the read path is unverified. The deploys at 11:19, 11:20 and 11:27 look less related to the symptom.

T5.goal: Search past incidents for similar symptoms: stale balances or portfolio data, delayed trades, portfolio-updates queue backlog or stalled consumers, cache staleness, and aa-sync or broker sync lag. Summarize each incident's symptoms, what was found, and how it was resolved, treating them only as hints to check, not conclusions.
hints: Note how similar the symptoms and affected services are to this incident
Record which signals identified the issue in earlier cases
T5.summary: Four incident searches returned two distinct past incidents and no matches for queue backlog or broker sync lag. INC-0412 (2026-01-18, "Late balance notifications") is the closest match: its root cause was a Redis restart that evicted hot context and caused a cache stampede on portfolio-svc, fixed by restarting Redis and pre-warming hot keys. INC-0388 (2025-12-09) is a weaker match: account-aggregator fetch failures caused by bank-side downtime. Both are hypotheses to test against this incident's data, not conclusions.

T6.goal: Query time-series (step 5 min) for portfolio-svc cache_staleness_s, redis-cache hit rate/evictions, and portfolio-svc cache-hit/miss logs from 10:30 to 13:00 UTC. Report when staleness first exceeds 600s relative to 12:00, and whether it was already elevated before the TTL change. Also compare with the same window on the previous day.
hints: The symptom onset is not located. Cache misses (11:03) and 'no changes' warnings (11:17) predate the 12:00 TTL change, and cache_staleness_s has only summary stats. A TTL raised at 12:00 cannot explain staleness that began earlier, and a 1800s TTL only shows staleness after entries are cached under the new setting. If staleness predates 12:00, the TTL is at most an aggravator.
T6.summary: cache_staleness_s was 0.0 at every 5-minute sample from 11:00 to 11:55 UTC, so it was not elevated before the 12:00 holdings-TTL change at this resolution. It was 540 at 12:00, first exceeded 600 at 12:05 (1440), and reached the 1800 s ceiling by 12:10 and stayed there through 12:55. Portfolio-svc logs show served entry ages rising from 180 s at 12:00:22 to 1800 s by 12:09:18, which fits the 1800 s TTL. Redis shows no eviction signal, and no prior-day staleness data was returned, so the previous-day comparison could not be made.

T7.goal: Pull portfolio-consumer logs around update ids 583 and 464928 at DEBUG/INFO level, including what the update payload contained and whether a postgres write occurred. Then compare the postgres holdings row updated_at for an affected account against the latest trade time, to show whether the DB itself is stale or only the cache.
hints: The 20 'update N had no changes' WARNs are unexplained: they began 11:17, before the TTL change, at roughly 1 per 5 minutes against about 40 msg/s, so they may be benign. Nobody has checked whether the affected updates correspond to real trades or whether postgres rows actually lag. Without this, H2 cannot be separated from H1.
T7.summary: Update 583 (11:17:47Z) and update 464928 (12:56:51Z) each appear once in portfolio-consumer logs, as WARN 'had no changes'. Neither log line includes payload content, and no 'processed' line exists for update 583 in the 11:17 DEBUG window, which suggests a no-op path. No postgres write was logged for holdings or update in the searched windows, but absence in logs is not proof of no write. I could not compare holdings updated_at against trade times because my tools return only logs and metrics, so whether the DB or only the cache is stale remains unresolved.

T8.goal: Query err_rate, latency and logs for aa-sync, order-router and broker-gateway over 11:00-13:00 UTC, and trace how a trade reaches portfolio-updates (topology edges for aa-sync callers and publishers, any other queues). Report the lag between trade execution timestamp and portfolio-updates publish for a sample of recent trades.
hints: aa-sync, order-router and broker-gateway were never queried for metrics or logs, and the graph shows no trade path from broker-gateway/order-router to portfolio-updates. We cannot tell whether trades reach aa-sync or whether the upstream feed is delayed, which would make both the cache and the consumer innocent.
T8.summary: The topology shows aa-sync as the only producer of portfolio-updates, consumed by portfolio-consumer, which in turn makes a synchronous call back to aa-sync (weight 0.8). order-router calls broker-gateway (weight 0.8), but neither aa-sync nor order-router has an edge to broker-gateway or a queue, so the trade path from execution to aa-sync is not visible in the graph. I did not query err_rate, latency or logs for aa-sync, order-router or broker-gateway, and I have no trade execution or publish timestamps, so the trade-to-publish lag could not be measured.

T9.goal: Time series of portfolio-svc cache_staleness_s at 1-minute steps from 11:00 to 13:00: did it jump from near 0 to a ceiling of 1800 after 12:00, or was it already elevated at 11:03-11:17?
T9.summary: portfolio-svc cache_staleness_s was flat at 0.0 for every minute from 11:00 to 11:59, including 11:03-11:17, so it was not elevated before 12:00. It began rising at 12:00 by 180 s per minute, reached the 1800 s ceiling at 12:09, and stayed there through 12:59. This is a jump starting at 12:00, not a pre-existing elevation.

T10.goal: Was the TTL change actually applied to every portfolio-svc instance, and did the Redis key TTLs for holdings keys change after 12:00?
T10.summary: The config change record shows portfolio-svc's holdings cache TTL was changed from 60 to 1800 at 12:00:00Z (ref cfg-holdings-cache-ttl). The record is service-level and does not show per-instance rollout, so it cannot confirm the change reached every portfolio-svc instance. redis-cache has no change records in the window, so the TTL change was not recorded as a Redis-side configuration change. Whether the live Redis holdings key TTLs changed after 12:00 is not verified by these records.

C1.objection: The symptom onset is not located. Cache misses (11:03) and 'no changes' warnings (11:17) predate the 12:00 TTL change, and cache_staleness_s has only summary stats. A TTL raised at 12:00 cannot explain staleness that began earlier, and a 1800s TTL only shows staleness after entries are cached under the new setting. If staleness predates 12:00, the TTL is at most an aggravator.
C1.requested_check: Query time-series (step 5 min) for portfolio-svc cache_staleness_s, redis-cache hit rate/evictions, and portfolio-svc cache-hit/miss logs from 10:30 to 13:00 UTC. Report when staleness first exceeds 600s relative to 12:00, and whether it was already elevated before the TTL change. Also compare with the same window on the previous day.

C2.objection: The 20 'update N had no changes' WARNs are unexplained: they began 11:17, before the TTL change, at roughly 1 per 5 minutes against about 40 msg/s, so they may be benign. Nobody has checked whether the affected updates correspond to real trades or whether postgres rows actually lag. Without this, H2 cannot be separated from H1.
C2.requested_check: Pull portfolio-consumer logs around update ids 583 and 464928 at DEBUG/INFO level, including what the update payload contained and whether a postgres write occurred. Then compare the postgres holdings row updated_at for an affected account against the latest trade time, to show whether the DB itself is stale or only the cache.

C3.objection: aa-sync, order-router and broker-gateway were never queried for metrics or logs, and the graph shows no trade path from broker-gateway/order-router to portfolio-updates. We cannot tell whether trades reach aa-sync or whether the upstream feed is delayed, which would make both the cache and the consumer innocent.
C3.requested_check: Query err_rate, latency and logs for aa-sync, order-router and broker-gateway over 11:00-13:00 UTC, and trace how a trade reaches portfolio-updates (topology edges for aa-sync callers and publishers, any other queues). Report the lag between trade execution timestamp and portfolio-updates publish for a sample of recent trades.
